name: speakers
title: Find speakers
description: Finds who speaks when in a video, gives each voice a pattern file and a sample to listen to, and names the voices it knows from earlier runs. No language model.

find.description: Finds who speaks when in a video, with no language model. Each voice gets an id (voice-1, voice-2...), a pattern (voice.json) and a sample to listen to. Type a name in a pattern and give it back in voices the next time: the turns of that voice then carry the name, and the pattern learns from the new speech.
find.title: Find speakers

media.title: Video or sound
media.description: The video or sound: a stored file or a video as media.open gives it, or a path in text. Loomas decodes its sound to 16 kHz, one channel.

voices.title: Known voices
voices.description: Voice patterns from earlier runs: the folder of a voice (with its voice.json), the voice.json itself, or its content. A voice that matches one takes its name.

maxSpeakers.title: Most speakers
maxSpeakers.description: The most voices to report; 0 lets the plugin decide (default 0).

minSimilarity.title: Least similarity to name a voice
minSimilarity.description: How similar a voice must be to a known pattern to take its name, from 0.1 to 1 (default 0.5).

learn.title: Learn known voices
learn.description: Let a known pattern learn from the new speech of its voice (default true). The pattern you gave is not changed: the result has the learned copy.

learnSimilarity.title: Least similarity to learn
learnSimilarity.description: How similar a voice must be to its pattern for the pattern to learn from it; at least minSimilarity (default 0.65). Higher keeps a doubtful match from changing a pattern.

files.title: Write the voice files
files.description: Write voice.json and a sample WAV for each voice (default true).

sampleMs.title: Longest sample
sampleMs.description: The longest sample of a voice (default 8000).

device.title: Run on
device.description: Where the models run: cpu (the default), or gpu / auto, which use the graphics card (on Windows, any DirectX 12 card). A card that cannot be used falls back to the processor; the result says what ran.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: When each voice speaks, in the order the turns start. Two voices can speak at once.

label.title: Speaker
label.description: The name of a known voice, or its id.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the speech model was, on average over the turn.

voices.title: Voices
voices.description: One for each voice heard, in the order they first speak.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of its pattern, or null for a voice nobody named yet.

known.title: Known
known.description: Whether it matched a pattern given in voices.

similarity.title: Similarity
similarity.description: How similar it was to its pattern, or null.

learned.title: Learned
learned.description: Whether its pattern learned from this video.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: The content of its voice.json: kind, format, model, id, name, seconds, print.

patternFile.title: Pattern file
patternFile.description: voice.json as a stored file. Left out when files is false.

sample.title: Sample
sample.description: A WAV of the voice to listen to. Left out when files is false.

device.title: What it ran on
device.description: What the voice print model really ran on: device, name (the graphics card, if one was used) and fallback (why not). Null when there was no sound.

failures.description: A param is wrong, a voice pattern is not one (or comes from another model), or media is missing or not sound Loomas decoded for the plugin.
A voice pattern file is not there.
A file cannot be read, the model cannot be loaded, or there is no folder for the voice files.
A model could not be downloaded (they are fetched once, on first use). Trying again may work.
